title: Gulveer Singh Becomes First Indian To Win Two Athletics Medals at a Single Commonwealth Games
excerpt: The Army runner claimed silver in the 10,000m and bronze in the 5,000m at Glasgow 2026, marking a historic breakthrough for Indian distance running on the global stage.
body:
• Gulveer Singh won silver in the 10,000m and bronze in the 5,000m at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games
  • He is the first Indian athlete to win two athletics medals at a single CWG edition
  • The Army Naib Subedar holds national records in both the 5,000m (12:59.77) and 10,000m (27:00.22)
  • His double medal haul signals India's growing competitiveness in distance running events

Gulveer Singh etched his name into Indian athletics history at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, becoming the first Indian to win two athletics medals at a single edition of the quadrennial event. The 27-year-old Army Naib Subedar from Atrauli, Uttar Pradesh, claimed silver in the 10,000m before adding a bronze in the 5,000m on August 1.

A Race for the Record Books

In the 5,000m final, Gulveer clocked a strong time to finish third behind Kenya's Kipsang, who took gold, and Australia's Ky Robinson, who earned silver. The bronze was India's first medal in the 5,000m at the CWG in over a decade.

His earlier silver in the 10,000m had already set the tone for a remarkable Games. Gulveer, who holds the national record in the event at 27:00.22, ran a tactically astute race, positioning himself in the leading pack through the middle laps before surging in the final two kilometres.

"I came here to win medals for India. Two medals in one Games is beyond what I imagined, but I knew I had the fitness for it."

— Gulveer Singh, Indian distance runner

From Army Barracks to the World Stage

Gulveer's journey from an Army athletics program to the Commonwealth podium reflects India's emerging depth in distance running. He burst onto the international scene by becoming the first Indian to run a sub-60-minute half marathon, a benchmark that had eluded Indian runners for years. His national records in the 5,000m (12:59.77) and 10,000m demonstrate a consistency rare among South Asian distance runners.

The Indian Army's sports programme has been a pipeline for middle- and long-distance talent, and Gulveer is its latest and most decorated product. His training regimen, managed by Army coaches with exposure to high-altitude camps, has given him the aerobic base to compete against East African and Australian rivals who typically dominate these events.

India's Athletics Renaissance

Gulveer's double medal haul is part of a broader uptick in Indian athletics at the Commonwealth Games. India's track and field contingent has been steadily improving, with javelin, shot put, and now distance events producing consistent international-level performers.

For the Indian diaspora, especially those who grew up watching India struggle in track and field, the achievement carries particular resonance. Distance running has historically been dominated by Kenyan, Ethiopian, and Australian athletes at the CWG, and an Indian breaking into the medals in both events is a statement of intent.

What's Next

Gulveer will now turn his attention to the 2027 World Athletics Championships and the build-up to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. His CWG double suggests he has the range and tactical maturity to compete at the highest level, and Indian athletics officials are expected to invest further in his programme. At 27, he is entering his prime years for distance running, and the Glasgow performance may be just the beginning.
